The present claim petition filed under section 166 & 140 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 was decided
by my learned predecessor vide ex-parte judgment dated 04.10.2013, whereby a compensation of
Rs.5,72,400/- with interest @ 7.5% per annum was awarded in favour of the petitioner from the
date of filing of petition till realization and further, respondent no.3/ The New India Assurance Co.
Ltd.

had been granted recovery rights against respondent no.1/ driver and respondent no.2/
registered owner of the offending vehicle.

under Order Ix Rule 13 Cpc for setting aside the ex-parte award dated 04.10.2013.

The application
was registered separately vide Misc Dj no. 96/2018.

Vide order dated 27.07.2018 my learned
predecessor observed that application was supported by Gpa, Dl, Registration Certificate, Fitness
Certificate and Permit of offending vehicle of which violation recovery rights were granted to
Insurance Company to deposit award amount and to recovery from the owner as well as driver and
it would be injustice to respondent no.2, if recovery rights are granted against her despite carrying
all necessary documents.

Accordingly, the award dated 04.10.2013 was set-aside on the limited
ground qua recovery rights of insurance company qua respondent no.2 and claim petition was

Further, it was held that the rest award shall remain intact as there was no dispute of

3.
In view of above, claim case was restored and respondent no.2 was allowed to lead evidence.

In
her evidence, with a view to disprove the violation of insurance policy, respondent no.2 got
examined R2W2 Sh. Dev Dutt, Regional Inspector, Uttar Pradesh Transport Department, Agra,
U.P., who produced the necessary documents in respect of the offending vehicle.

Then, the evidence
was closed.

4. I have heard the arguments addressed by learned counsel for the respondent no.2 and learned
counsel for insurance company and perused the evidence and other relevant documents placed on
record.

5. I may note that on the issue of liability, my learned predecessor, vide judgment dated 04.10.2013,
observed that despite notice under Order 12 rule 8 Cpc, sent to respondent no.2, she failed to
produce the permit and hence, it can be inferred that she was not having valid and effective permit

Further, it was held that the Insurance
Company shall initially satisfy the award and thereafter, it shall be entitled to recover the awarded
amount from the respondent no.1 & 2.
6.

There is no dispute regarding the award amount which is still intact and the only dispute under
adjudication now is with respect to the recovery rights of insurance company against respondent
no.2.

In order to prove that she was having valid and effective Fitness Certificate and Permit in
respect of offending vehicle on the date accident (21.04.2009), respondent no.2 got examined R2W2
Sh. Dev Dutt, Regional Inspector, Uttar Pradesh Transport Department, Agra, U.P.

During his
evidence, R2W2 placed on record the following documents relating to offending vehicle be
aring registration no. UP80-AN- 9525:-

sentences.text:
Fitness Certificate Receipts bearing numbers:-
(a). Receipt no. 26145, for 01.10.2007 to 30.09.2008.
Tourist Permit Receipt bearing no. 395901, dated 20.09.2005, for the period from 21.09.2005 to 20.09.2010.
(iii). Adhikar Patra, bearing no. 607/STA/2023, dated 27.04.2023.
The aforesaid documents placed on record by R2W2 are found duly attested by the Assistant Regional Transport Officer, (Administration), Agra.

Perusal of fitness certificate receipts mentioned at serial no. (i)(b) above makes it clear that the receipt no. 37372 was generated for the fitness certificate, issued from the concerned transport authority in respect of the offending vehicle bearing no.UP80-AN-9525 for the period from 15.10.2008 to 14.10.2009, which would mean that the said fitness certificate in respect of the offending vehicle was valid and effective on the date of accident i.e. 21.04.2009.

Further, perusal of copy of Tourist Permit Receipt, duly attested by ARTO, Agra,
mentioned above at serial no. (ii) shows that the prescribed fee was collected by the concerned Transport Department vide receipt no. 395901 on dated 20.09.2005 for issuing All India Tourist Permit in respect of the offending vehicle bearing no.UP80-AN-9525.
Further, I may observe that nothing contrary has come during cross-examination of R2W2 conducted by learned counsel for insurance company to doubt the documentary evidence led by the witness.

8. In view of above, the respondent no.2 by examining R2W2, who relied upon the necessary record of fitness certificates and permit of the offending vehicle, in my opinion, has been able to prove on record that respondent no.2 was having valid and effective fitness certificate and Permit in respect o f t h e o f f e n d i n g v e h i c l e o n t h e d a t e o f a c c i d e n t . V i d e _____________________________________________________________________ MACT no. 51173/10 (Old no. 1173/10) 5 of 6 Pages order dated 04.10.2013, my learned predecessor had set-aside the ex-parte award dated 04.10.2013 and allowed the respondent no.2 to lead evidence to disprove the violation of insurance policy and I find that the respondent no.2 has been successful in discharging the said onus, as discussed above.

Therefore, since the respondent no.2 was having valid and effective fitness certificate and permit with respect to the offending vehicle, it is held that respondent no.2 has been able to prove that there was no breach of any terms and conditions of the insurance policy.

Accordingly, it is held that the recovery rights granted to the respondent no.3/ The New India Assurance Co. Ltd. vide ex- parte award dated 04.10.2013 are hereby recalled and rest of the award shall remain intact.
